spec: Write mdtable.py with two functions for GitHub-flavoured Markdown pipe tables. `parse(md: str) -> tuple[list[str], list[str], list[list[str]]]` returns (headers, aligns, rows): leading/trailing pipes are optional, cells are stripped, `\|` inside a cell is a literal pipe, the delimiter row decides alignment per column (`:--` left, `:-:` center, `--:` right, `---` "none"), rows shorter than the header are padded with "" and longer rows are truncated; raise ValueError if the second line is not a valid delimiter row or its column count differs from the header. Lines before the header are ignored (the header is the first line containing a pipe), and the table ends at the first blank line or end of text; anything after it is ignored. `render(headers, aligns, rows) -> str` writes a table back with leading and trailing pipes, cells escaped first (`|` -> `\|`), each column padded to its widest escaped cell (minimum width 3) and justified by its alignment (right -> right-justified, center -> str.center, left/none -> left-justified), one space between each pipe and cell, delimiter cells like `:---`, `:---:`, `---:`, `---` each exactly as long as the column width including the colons (width 3 right -> `--:`), lines joined with \n and no trailing newline. parse(render(h, a, r)) must round-trip. Standard library only.
